body.statement: Determine \(\mathcal R(n,m,\tau)\) up to constants depending only on \(\beta,D\) for every joint sequence \(n\to\infty\), even \(m=m_n\ge2\), and \(0<\tau_n\le1/(8n)\). The answer must identify every unavoidable logarithmic factor, give a necessary-and-sufficient joint-sequence criterion for \(\mathcal R(n,m,\tau)\to0\), construct a computable \(\widehat\pi_{\mathrm{tail}}\) attaining the frontier, and prove a same-class lower bound against \(\mathfrak A_{n,m}\) that remains sharp through sparse-dominance, collective-contribution, and local-to-tied regimes. Express the answer as strict comparisons with both named baselines. In the dense reallocating regime \(m\to\infty\), \(m\log(2m)=o(n)\), and \(\mathcal B_{\mathrm{CK}}(n,m,\tau)\to0\), identify the maximal subregimes on which capacity averaging gives \(\mathcal R(n,m,\tau)=o\{\mathcal B_{\mathrm{CK}}(n,m,\tau)\}\) and the complementary subregimes on which the coordinatewise bound is unavoidable. Across every vanishing-regret regime, quantify the separation from \(\mathcal B_{\mathrm{AW}}(n,m)\) rather than importing a regular-policy penalty.
body.justification: The lower-side missed-cell distribution and amplitude optimization are now proved; the remaining headline contribution is a matching full-class capacity-aware learner or a harder same-class lower configuration.
body.gap: CarpentierKim2015 supplies translated one-tail Hall machinery but no randomized product-class capacity oracle inequality, and AtheyWager2021 supplies no moving extreme-mixture rate.
body.consumer: Completion would give the non-nested upper-cost-quantile objective of OsamaZachariahStoica2020 an explicit Hall extrapolation boundary; that paper does not itself provide the boundary.

obligation.what_is_open: Match the proved multiscale paired-splice lower envelope with one computable full-class capacity-aware learner in every sparse, collective, and local-to-tied regime, or prove that another same-class configuration is harder.
obligation.obstruction: The distributional converse is no longer the gap. The missing step is an upper oracle inequality controlling data-dependent selected mixture weights under rare severe tail-index underestimation without using a coordinatewise maximum; the only verified learner pays \([\log(2m)]^{\varkappa}\).
obligation.attempted: I completed the fixed-sample posterior factorization, capacity exchange, binomial stochastic lower bound, and amplitude optimization. I then tried a natural-threshold empirical minimizer and an average multiplicative core comparison. Neither controls selection of a severely underestimated heavy arm, whereas imposing simultaneous control reproduces the existing familywise upper rate.
obligation.partial_result:
Put \(A_{n,m,\tau}:=\ell\min\{1,N^{-\varkappa}\}\) and \(L_m:=\log(2m)\).  The proved bounds now include
\[
c_{\beta,D}\min\!\left\{\ell,\;
A_{n,m,\tau}\left[1+\min\!\left\{
A_{n,m,\tau}^{\varkappa/(1-\varkappa)},L_m^{\varkappa}
\right\}\right]\right\}
\leq\mathcal R(n,m,\tau)
\leq C_{\beta,D}\mathcal B_{\mathrm{CK}}(n,m,\tau).
\]
The lower proof retains the exact identity
\[
4h=\log\left[1+\frac Hm\{e^{\delta(b+h)}-1\}\right]
\]
and replaces the mean-only Assouad step by a binomial stochastic lower bound for \(H\), valid after unrestricted capacity reallocation and for testing information from order one through order \(\log m\).  This proves the constant-information, intermediate, and familywise lower phases.  What remains unknown is whether a computable learner over the full heterogeneous Hall class attains this envelope, or whether a harder heterogeneous configuration raises it.
